title: QNAP MCP Assistant per-user auth integration

scope.defaultDecision: Use the official QNAP MCP Assistant as the preferred/default integration path when its client launch, per-user auth, and safe tool exposure requirements are met; keep the existing first-party pros-mcp-qnap-files bridge as documented fallback for bounded case-file workflows.
scope.thinWrapperDecision: Do not reimplement QNAP File Station. Add only Pros-side client-config metadata, policy documentation, and tests. Use a thin wrapper/filter only if official Assistant tooling cannot block silent upload/overwrite/delete or client compatibility fails.
scope.nasBoundaryDecision: QNAP user permissions are the NAS boundary. Do not bind official Assistant usage to local cwd, workspace, or fallordner.

implementationTasks.summary: Extend MCP client configuration to include a QNAP MCP Assistant include target for OpenCode and AnythingLLM.
acceptance: Generated entries contain command/args only and no credentials or tokens.
OpenCode and AnythingLLM QNAP entries do not set cwd or fallordner-like path allowlists.
Managed state and status checks understand qnap-mcp-assistant.

implementationTasks.summary: Encode tool-surface classification and safety policy for official Assistant default versus Pros fallback.
acceptance: Repo artifact classifies read, transfer, write, destructive, and admin/system capabilities.
Silent delete/overwrite/upload is rejected by policy; preview/approval or blocking is required.
No admin/system NAS functions are documented as default user workflow.

implementationTasks.summary: Update runtime manifest, setup workflow, CLI docs, tracker, and reference docs.
acceptance: Docs mention nasproselect.myqnapcloud.com, per-user auth, no-secret config, QNAP user permissions, no cwd/fallordner binding, and preview/approval.
Runtime manifest marks official QNAP MCP Assistant as preferred/default with fallback conditions.

implementationTasks.summary: Add and run tests for client config, QNAP MCP surface, no-secret policy, and live-smoke blocked handling.
acceptance: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm test pass or failures are documented with root cause.
Secret scan over changed files finds no QNAP password, token, or session material.
Live smoke is PASS with redacted user context or BLOCKED due to missing credentials; no simulation.

assumptions: No live internal QNAP credentials are available in this chat/session unless explicitly supplied out-of-band by the user.
The official QNAP MCP Assistant may not be locally installed; implementation must document/install-configure without storing secrets.
Existing first-party pros-mcp-qnap-files remains a safe fallback and should not be loosened for NAS-wide official Assistant behavior.

alternativesConsidered.option: Official QNAP MCP Assistant as direct default
alternativesConsidered.reason: Officially maintained surface, lower custom code burden, supports per-user Assistant-style workflows if auth is local/per-user and config is secret-free.

alternativesConsidered.option: First-party Pros File Station bridge as default
alternativesConsidered.reason: Already safer and preview-only, but intentionally bounded by profiles/share allowlists and unsuitable for NAS-wide per-user chat workflows.

alternativesConsidered.option: Thin Pros wrapper/filter around official Assistant
alternativesConsidered.reason: Use only if official Assistant exposes silent destructive tools or client incompatibilities; avoids speculative wrapper code.

metaReview.notes: Reviews include source plan, user completion criteria, existing qnap-files fallback, MCP client config, runtime manifest, docs, tests, secret scan, and live-smoke blocked path.

overEngineeringReview.notes: No new QNAP HTTP client or full wrapper is planned unless official Assistant safety constraints fail. Minimal config/docs/tests changes are preferred.

planGate.userConfirmation: accepted from Ralph Phase 0 per user instruction
